answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a violet as the anchor of the cost.
